summary:
ClauseClock Stage 1 GATE verification PASSED. All 5 deliberately-difficult text-based fixtures extracted correctly with usable location markers, and the image-only scanned PDF was flagged with the EXACT scanned message. Full hard-delete of every created contract confirmed; GridFS fs.files, contracts and documents collections all returned to 0 after the run.

Per-fixture results:
- GATE 1 gate_docx.docx: PASS — extraction_method=python-docx, raw_text contains '[§' (heading), '¶' (paragraph) and '[Table' markers; '$24,000' fee and 'Appendix A' content present.
- GATE 2 gate_twocol.pdf: PASS — extraction_method=pdfplumber, page_count=3, 'Page 1/2/3' markers present, 'automatically renew', 'sixty (60)' and 'certified mail' all readable (column interleaving accepted per Stage-1 spec).
- GATE 3 gate_40pages.pdf: PASS — page_count>=40 with >=40 distinct 'Page N' markers, extraction_method=pdfplumber.
- GATE 4 gate_appendix.pdf: PASS — 'APPENDIX B', '$48,000' and 'capped at eight percent (8%)' all appear after the 'Page 2' marker.
- GATE 5 gate_tables.pdf: PASS — '[Table' marker present and every required cell (Bronze, $24,000, Gold, $48,000, Cap %) readable.
- SCANNED GUARDRAIL gate_scanned.pdf: PASS — extraction_method=failed_no_text, extraction_warnings contains EXACT message. GET /api/contracts/{id} surfaces the same and raw_text is effectively empty (only auto-inserted 'Page N' delimiters remain, no content).
- Cleanup: PASS — every created contract deleted (200 + deleted:true), subsequent GET returns 404, contracts list empty, GridFS fs.files count restored (0 after run).
critical_code_review_comments: ingestion.py: _extract_pdf appends the '========== Page N ==========' delimiter for every page regardless of whether any text was extracted. For a scanned/image-only PDF this means document.raw_text ends up as pure page markers with no content — technically not empty. Not a functional bug (extraction_method=failed_no_text and the exact SCANNED_MESSAGE are the contract used by the frontend), but consider suppressing the page-marker skeleton when is_scanned() triggers so raw_text is truly empty and downstream text-length heuristics can't be misled.

pytest.ini enables xdist loadscope by default. Module-scoped fixtures in xdist run once per worker, which broke a strict GridFS baseline assertion (baseline captured on one worker, cleanup ran on another). Non-blocking — test-side fix applied by running the gate module without xdist and by belt-and-braces purging any dangling TEST_gate contracts before the baseline assertion.
seed_data_creation: None persisted — every TEST_gate_* contract created during the run is hard-deleted at end of module; verified via list API + Mongo counts (fs.files=0, contracts=0, documents=0).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the gate suite with:  python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_clauseclock_gate.py -v -o addopts=''  (bypass the project pytest.ini xdist config, since the module has a module-scoped GridFS baseline fixture and a terminal cleanup class that must all run in the same worker). Fixtures live at /app/backend/tests/gate_*. Seeded test user 'test@clauseclock.app' / 'Test1234!'. Storage is GridFS (fs.files/fs.chunks); hard-delete route removes originals. Scanned detection uses <100 chars/page and returns the EXACT SCANNED_MESSAGE constant from ingestion.py.
rca of the issue: N/A — gate verification only. No functional bugs found. All 5 text-based fixtures produced readable extracted text with usable location markers and the scanned guardrail returns the exact required message.
